memory_candidates.content: In constructive/intuitionistic modal-logic canonical completeness, a frame condition can be genuinely WEAKENED to make soundness hold and completeness EASIER without weakening the logic: task 509's cs5FC'' drops task 508's cs5FCweak defect (it omitted plain symmetry r w u -> r u w, the exact clause the bDia axiom needs) and adds it back. A published 'this cannot be done by canonical-model work' negative verdict was refuted purely by locating one missing frame clause. Lesson: when a soundness-side impossibility claim rests on a specific candidate frame condition, audit that condition clause-by-clause against each axiom before accepting the impossibility.

When porting a published proof into a proof assistant, treat the primeness/maximality lemma as the highest-risk step: Pacheco 2024's Lemma 16 (reused by his pair-Zorn Lemma 18) derives primeness from 'phi not in Theta => not-phi in Theta', which is negation-completeness and is unsound for prime/quasi-prime theories in a constructive setting. The correct pattern derives the disjunction property from poset-invariant violations under maximality (as CSLib's set_maximal_is_prime does for the one-sided Lindenbaum case), never from negation-completeness. Plan a dedicated repair phase for any imported primeness-from-maximality step rather than transcribing it on faith.
